subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - GPU sizing & SLOs

Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - GPU sizing & SLOs

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Recap (from our convo)
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for short responses (~64 tokens), p95 <= 400ms for 512-token generations.
- Throughput/concurrency: product expects ~500 concurrent users at peak, steady-state traffic equivalent to ~60 requests/sec (in terms of full-model calls), with spiky bursts up to 200 rps for short windows.
- Streaming: client requires partial-token streaming (server push) for chat UX; must preserve per-token latency and support connection keep-alive semantics.
- Model family: you mentioned using a 70B variant with FP16/HF16 weights; team currently evaluates both A100 and H100-backed instances.

What we need from you to scope a dedicated validation run
1) Recent perf numbers (p50/p95/p99) under your internal load test for the model variant and batch sizes you expect.
2) Target traffic profile (percent chat vs batch, average tokens per request, % of streaming sessions).
3) Any constraints for warm KV cache or prompt-engineering quirks (e.g., long context windows, many reused prefixes).
4) Preferred week for a live canary/validation (we suggested w/c Jul 19 on the call).

Proposed Redwood validation plan
- Baseline test on A100 and H100 configurations with identical model artifacts and input profile.
- Reserved throughput targets: start with 50 rps reserved per GPU pool and scale to match your requested concurrency; we'll size number of GPUs accordingly and present tradeoffs (cost vs latency headroom).
- Success criteria: p95 latency under load within 1.1x of your target (i.e., <= 275ms for short responses), stable CPU/GPU utilization < 75% at steady-state, no request timeouts under burst.
- Canary run: 2-day validation with canary routing, synthetic load + a small percentage of real traffic if you permit.

Next steps
- Can you send the internal perf CSVs and a short traffic profile doc?
- Confirm if Jul 19 works for a validation run.

Attachments: please attach any perf CSVs (we recommended a simple schema) — we'll ingest and run Redwood sizing suggestions ahead of the canary.

Best,

Thanks Neha — appreciate the recap. Attaching our most recent internal perf dump (acme_benchmark_results.csv). Quick highlights from our measurements on 70B model (FP16) under our controller-based runner:
- A100 (40GB)
  - 1 GPU sustained: ~60 req/s (512-token gen), p50=120ms, p95=220ms, p99=450ms (batching=auto, async streaming disabled)
- H100 (80GB)
  - 1 GPU sustained: ~85 req/s (512-token gen), p50=90ms, p95=180ms, p99=360ms
- Concurrency: clients currently open ~500 concurrent chat sessions during peak (approx 65% of sessions trigger full model generation; rest are short-lived metadata calls).
- Streaming: we do partial-token streaming today using a push model. We need token-level latency to be <30ms for token emission after generation step.

Notes: the CSV contains per-run batch sizes, sequence lengths, and measured latency percentiles. We generated these tests with synthetic user mixes; I'll share the SRE runbook separately if helpful.

We are interested in validating both A100 and H100 options. Jul 19 week works for us; prefer Jul 20/21 for the canary.

-Alex

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - GPU sizing & SLOs

Alex — got the CSV, thanks for the fast turnaround. I reviewed a few runs and sketched an initial sizing proposal below.

Initial sizing notes (rough):
- If we target your prod SLO of p95 <= 250ms for 64-token responses and p95 <= 400ms for 512-token responses, H100 provides more headroom per GPU (based on your numbers ~85 rps vs 60 rps on A100).
- Reserved throughput approach: we can reserve a pool sized to handle steady 60 rps with headroom for bursts. For your 500 concurrent chat users, assuming 65% model invocations and average think-time ~6s, that maps to ~54 sustained rps — so a pool of 1 H100 or 1.5 A100 equivalent (we'll round to whole GPUs) is the starting point; for peak bursts we recommend autoscaling delta of +2 GPUs.
- Streaming: Redwood supports token streaming; we'll validate token emission latency end-to-end. Token-level <30ms requirement is achievable on H100 with tuned kernel/IO stack; we'll validate in the canary.

Proposed validation plan (concrete)
- Day 0: ingest your CSV and map test cases to Redwood workload profiles.
- Day 1: baseline runs on A100 and H100 (1 GPU each) using synthetic traffic matching your mix; collect p50/p95/p99 and token emission times.
- Day 2: scale to reserved pool sizing (as described) and run longer soak tests; run streaming tests with 10% of traffic using real sessions (if you approve).
- Deliverable: bench report + recommended committed GPU counts + cost estimate + canary playbook.

Can you confirm:
- That Jul 20/21 are ok for the two validation run days?
- Whether SRE can accept a small fraction (10%) of real traffic during Day 2?
- Any additional success criteria (e.g., sustained 95th percentile error rate < 0.1%)?

If that looks good I’ll have Marissa put together a draft proposal/quote and we’ll book the canary slots.

Thanks,
